GHz WiFi connection, which the vast majority of routers have, typically being dual band along with a 5.0 GHz connection. The reason that there are two bands is that while the 5.0 frequency is super-fast (best for streaming videos and online video games), the 2.4 frequency has a longer range (better for connecting to outdoor electronics, e.g., your Pro 575). Of course, like any other devices that use WiFi, there can be other factors that may need to be considered, such as firewalls/VPNs, distance from the router and how old the software version is on the phone or tablet being used. Luckily, Traeger Customer Service has access to a third party app that can analyze your home network and determine what might be preventing the grill from connecting. ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thanks for reviewing the Pro 780. Unlike other types of outdoor grills that cook with gas or charcoal, Traeger pellet grills cook entirely with burning wood. When in use, the only source of heat is burning pellets at the bottom of the grill, which will also create smoke at the same time. However, like any wood fire, the hotter/faster it burns, the less smoke will be created. This is why the slow and low method is used when trying to maximize smoke flavor. Keeping the temperature at 225 degrees or lower not only extends the time that food is exposed to the smoke, but it also greatly increases the production of blue smoke, which is the ultimate goal for any smoker. A little research online will provide a lot of information on why this barely visible blue smoke is so preferred for adding smoke flavor to food. There are also a couple of helpful articles on Traeger.com that you might find useful. Just search “smoke science” for one that goes over the basics of smoking, including the topic of blue smoke, and “not enough smoke” for some tips on maximizing smoke flavor. You can also call Traeger Support if you have more specific questions on the subject, or anything else related to your grill.
ClientResponses.Name: Traeger Grills

I purchased an after-market chimney cap and chimney pipe, they were not sold separately, and I only used the nuts and bolts from the new cap to secure the original chimney cap to the original chimney pipe. ClientResponses.Response: Hello, and thanks for posting your feedback on the Pro 780. If the grill is working some of the time, but not others, then it is probably a simple fix to resolve the issue. Assuming that the pellets have not become compromised, there are only so many things that can cause a grill to perform this way. The best thing to do in this situation is to call Traeger support when the grill is cold so that an agent can look over everything (via the camera on your smartphone) and do a quick test run with you. It usually only takes one call to resolve most issues, and you can reach us any day of the year, up until 10:00 PM MT.

Sometimes it heats up and sometimes it doesn’t - it’s not a reliable product (especially for the price) and in fact the most unreliable grill I’ve ever used. I plan on switching to another product.

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thanks for your review of the Pro 780. Although there can be some slight variation in temperature from one side to another, this will be found on just about any larger grill, but it should not be extreme. However, there are a few things that can increase the effect on pellet smokers, such as damage to internal components, as well as loose foil covering the tray. Even using large pans can disrupt airflow enough to magnify the issue if there is not at least an inch between the sides of the pan and the grill walls. As for having a surface to place utensils on, we do have a couple of solutions for you. The first is a folding shelf (part #BAC442) that can be attached to the front of the grill, providing a 32.5" x 11.6" surface to work with. There is also a 3 piece magnetic hook set (part #BAC536) that can be put on the side of the hopper for hanging your favorite utensils. And while it is true that the grill cannot be started remotely, this is actually an intentional safety design so that someone can confirm that the grill is safe to start (e.g., not covered, nothing inside, etc.) and to make sure that it is never turned on accidentally.
ClientResponses.Name: Traeger Grills

Results.ReviewText:
I would not recommend to a friend or buy again for myself, without considering other options. 
-- The left side (leftmost quarter predominantly) of the grill cooks 20-30 degrees hotter than the right. Clearly some oversight in the engineering. I have to plan my meals accordingly. 
-- The lack of an exterior surface or two to place utensils on a $1000 grill is beyond disappointing. Cannot overstate how frustrating it is to have no place to set a bowl, plate or grill utensil. Plan for another piece of furniture to make up for this.
--The inability to start the grill remotely is another bother, and fairly well hidden in their marketing of the WiFIRE capabilities. 
-- The cover is an additional ~$120 purchase
Consider other options, like Pit Boss for a better value.
Results.Title: Expensive for uneven temperature and no storage

ClientResponses.Response: Hi, and thanks for your review of the Pro 575. Based on your experience, your frustration is certainly understandable. While this kind of performance is typically not seen outside of extremely cold conditions, there can be some non-weather related causes, such as a chimney cap being set too low, keeping the lid open during startup, using pellets that are past their prime or having a buildup of dust in the bottom of the hopper. Of course, these are probably factors that you’ve already considered, but there is one thing that might be creating the opposite effect from what is intended. Adding pellets manually to prime the firepot can actually interfere with airflow and ultimately delay ignition. As long as the auger is fully primed before attempting a cook, there really should be no need to add more pellets by hand. But assuming that this was done because of the slow startups in the first place, it would only be aggravating the situation and not the initial cause. If you haven’t specifically done this already, consider reaching out to Traeger support while the grill is totally cooled down and let an agent do a thorough visual check of it through the camera on your cellphone. A lot of times, issues like this are resolved by something revealed before the grill is even turned on, and you never know what might be discovered.
ClientResponses.Name: Traeger Grills

Results.ReviewText:
I am redoing my rating of Traeger and my 575. At first I was angry and upset that my grill was not working as I thought it should. Well it turns out the Traeger grills are a totally different animal than any of the others out there. I am referring to BBQ's like wood, charcoal, propane, pellets, I have had them all! They all have their places. Let's start with wood, I love wood the smell, the flavor of wood smoked meat. Dislikes direct flame; which is to hard to keep a constant heat and not burn anything. Wood is also the best for smoking. Charcoal- works well for BBQ, even heat, taste is ok. Not able to smoke with charcoal unless you learn how to.  Propane- YEAH! I don't see the reason for it. If you are going to use gas for cooking why not put it on the stove or oven. I'm not a fan.
Now let's move to pellets- I have never heard of or used one. I was intrigued, it is a grill that uses wood yet there is no open flame. OK! I'll try. 
WOW! Traeger's are a little pricey compared to others out there. Let's see what all the fuss is about and the price.
I purchased  the middle of the road Traeger 575. I thankfully purchased it from our local ACE Hardware. They have almost everything you could want for your grill. I went a little crazy and purchased the cover, cleaner brush, the orange cleaner, liners for the BBQ and the drip can. I also purchased the best pellets so far. I have only tried three different ones. The best so far is the Signature, it goes with everything. 
So what I learned is the Traeger 575 wifi is a great grill! I would love to have purchased the Flagship but honestly it is way more grill than I would have ever used. There are a lot of great recipes on the app. The timer and meat thermometer work excellent. The temp of the 575 if cooking small items, like a couple of burgers, a steak and two potatoes', the temp is off a little. Now if you are using it full the temp is dead on. 
Now the grill and the directions tell you to clean your grill after every two to three uses or depending on how greasy the meal is. MAKE SURE TO CLEAN your grill. A quick vacuum and wipedown is all it takes. Make sure to use the tray liners, makes cleaning easy.
Now for the cooking. I got mine back in July and I have cooked everything I can at this grill. I have to say it is AWESOME! I cooked "bacon" Yes! bacon right on the grill. The bacon stayed the same shape as I put it on the grill and came out perfectly crispy. In fact it was so perfect, my wife thought it was fake. 
Everything and I mean everything came out wonderful. 
The strange thing to me is when your grill heats up and tells you it is ready, you open the lid and expect to have this huge wave if heat hit you in the face. It never does. As well as when you place your food on the grill, you expect to get burnt by the flame. There isn't one!
If you have never cooked with one you need to find someone with a Traeger and become friends. LOL!
Maybe you can go down to your local retailer that sells them and ask them to have a Traeger demo day! Here you go Traeger have someone who is familiar with cooking on a Traeger and have demo days on a weekend. Cook and have food for people to sample.
P.S. for smoking I have done a few things that help with more smoke. I adjusted the top hat down a little bit and turned the temp down. I get more smoke this way.
I do not work for Traeger nor are they paying, giving or promising me anything. I just really like my grill. Now I want the Flagship just to see what it is capable of. I also love to BBQ, so I am a little biased. I would rather be cooking outside than inside.

Results.OriginalProductName: Pro 575 Pellet Grill - Black
Results.ReviewText: DON'T BUY.  My grill will not go below 225-230 degrees regardless of the setting.  According to Traeger's troubleshooting guide it states if the ambient temperature is above 85 degrees the grill will not function below 225. In other words, you cannot smoke a brisket in the summer. After reading the MANY reviews this is a recognized problem with these grills. Move it to the shade it states.  Today and most any summer day in Texas it is around 90-100 degrees IN THE SHADE.   During the SUMMER is when you smoke briskets etc.  You cannot smoke a brisket at 225 degrees.  It was represented as a top of the line SMOKER by your dealer and the website.  I regret having purchased this grill as there was no disclaimer about not being able to smoke during the summer which is when you expect to use it.  Customer service wants to simply have you replace parts over and over.   I've replaced 2 previous controllers, two RCP's, cleaned the grill, fire pot, and lowered the smoke stack, and the meat probes read 30 degrees different from each other.  The very first day I used it the auger locked up and stripped the bolt that attaches to the motor.  I have had to do all the warranty work myself as no Traeger dealer will work on it, warranty or otherwise.  I am now realizing it is a DESIGN ISSUE as you sell this as a SMOKER....but it won't smoke during the summer when you need it.  If I had just wanted a GRILL I would have bought a grill which gets much hotter for grilling.  Last week they replaced the RCP.  This week I was assured it was the controller.  I found a new controller locally and bought it and it made no difference as I was hoping to smoke a brisket on the 4th of July.  It is a piece of junk IMHO.  THE PROBLEM is the DESIGN not faulty parts.  It simply will not stay below 225 degrees.  I wish I had my money back.  It will ruin a $60 brisket.  My oven cooks better than this.
Results.Title: PIECE of CRAP that will not smoke in the summer

I do love using my Traeger grill and I love the food it produces, however, there is a design flaw in my opinion.  

You've designed this great (and somewhat expensive) grill but the grease catcher is basically a bucket that just dangles.  If you cover your grill like I do, it makes it virtually impossible to take the cover off without 1) having to reach under the cover prior to removing the cover or 2) if you forget to do so, having that bucket fall off onto your deck and spill grease everywhere...every single time.  I guess you could replace the bucket liner after every use, but you can't cover the grill until you are sure that all of the grease is done dripping.  A more secure grease bucket would solve that problem.

If you end up using my idea, feel free to send me a Traeger tee shirt, or better yet, a coupon for my local rental store so I can rent a pressure washer and sander so I can get the grease stains out of my deck.
